title: Mughal Empire (1526-1857)
key_facts: Islamic imperial power that ruled most of Indian subcontinent
Known for architectural marvels: Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Fatehpur Sikri
Peak under Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, and Aurangzeb
Declined after Aurangzeb's religious intolerance and administrative overextension
causes: Babur's victory at Panipat established Mughal rule in India
Military superiority of Turco-Mongol cavalry and artillery
Administrative genius of Akbar's centralized bureaucracy
Control of lucrative trade routes and agricultural surplus
outcome: British East India Company exploited Mughal weakness
Indian Rebellion of 1857 ended formal Mughal rule
Legacy of syncretic Indo-Islamic culture and architecture

figures.name: Aurangzeb
figures.role: Last great Mughal emperor; orthodox Islam

impacts: Created unified Indo-Islamic culture and architectural heritage
Established centralized administration influencing later Indian states
Contributed to spread of Persian and Turkic culture in India
Left lasting impact on Indian art, music, literature, and cuisine
